gemini-2.5-flash.exact_reserve_text: We regret to advise that the 2022 year of account will close with a loss of GBP 29.3m or US$36.6m being 13.9% of Stamp capacity. 2022 YOA closing result: $36.6m Loss

prior_year_events.impact_description: A material increase in frequency of severe loss in our healthcare professional liability portfolio, which has emerged in the 2nd half year of 2024. We have increased reserves on all years. The 2022 and prior gross reserves were increased by GBP 21.3m, partially offset by increased reinsurance recoveries of GBP 4.7m.
Aviation war claims arising from the Russia/Ukraine conflict being settled on an ex-gratia basis in the 4th quarter 2024. The increase in reserve is GBP 12.8m gross, GBP 5.1m net of reinsurance.

prior_year_events.event_name: US General Liability contractor portfolio deterioration
prior_year_events.impact_description: Deterioration in our US General Liability contractor portfolio. have strengthened gross (and net) reserves by GBP 5.4m for the 2022 and prior years.

named_events.loss_description: The 2024 year has seen a continuation of the increase in global natural catastrophe losses which has reached $135bn for the industry. This has been driven by Hurricanes Helene and Milton which account for around $50bn, there has also been severe levels of flooding globally particularly in Europe. The impact to the Syndicate has been lessened by the improvement in pricing, attachment levels and terms and conditions that we have seen in the Property Treaty account. The impact of both hurricane events is less than $7.5m to this portfolio which also shows the impact of the remediation steps we took in 2023. Overall, the Syndicate total net loss to these events is less than $25m which is significantly within the Year of Account Net Cat Budget and shows the resilience of the portfolio to this level of loss activity.

The impact of the Los Angeles Wildfires are a timely reminder that catastrophe losses can happen at any time, our sympathies are with those that have been affected by this disaster. This loss has again highlighted the financial risks associated with perils that are closely linked to climate change. At the time the reserves were set we were aware of the expected loss in respect of the Los Angeles Wildfires and are therefore not expecting this to deteriorate the ultimate result for this year of account.
The Syndicate also experienced the largest individual gross loss ($21.6m) which impacted the Marine Reinsurance portfolio as result of the Baltimore bridge collapse.
Aviation war claims arising from the Russia/Ukraine conflict being settled on an ex-gratia basis in the 4th quarter 2024. The increase in reserve is GBP 12.8m gross, GBP 5.1m net of reinsurance.

This adverse development was primarily driven by a material increase in severe losses within the healthcare professional liability portfolio, aviation war claims arising from the Russia/Ukraine conflict, and deterioration in the US General Liability contractor portfolio. Inflation also remains a key concern impacting reserve strength.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Financial statements and technical reserves are presented in USD. Many narrative reserve movements are expressed in GBP; where the report supplied USD conversions (e.g. GBP 29.3m = US$36.6m) the USD figure was used. Several event-specific reserve changes are quantified in GBP only in the narrative; these were recorded as qualitative impacts (amounts left null) to avoid inaccurate conversions where no USD equivalent was provided. Opening gross claims outstanding and P&L technical amounts were taken from the Technical Provisions note and Statement of Profit or Loss (all in USD). Confidence levels reflect whether figures were explicitly stated (1.0), calculated from provided conversions (0.8), inferred from narrative (0.5-0.7), or not quantified (0.0).
